item.title: Brady ends association with Birmingham City
item.description: Brady brought an end to his illustrious NFL career in 2023 [Getty Images] NFL legend Tom Brady has ended his association with top-of-the-table Championship side Birmingham City. The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner in the St Andrew's club in August 2023 when he "entered a partnership" with club owners Knighthead Capital Management LLC. Part of Brady's role involved him being chairman of an advisory board at Birmingham, with the club saying he would be "both investing [as well as] committing his time and extensive expertise" following his arrival. However, the Blues announced his exit with a statement headlined 'Tom Brady departure'. They added: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. "It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community." Former quarterback Brady, a three-time NFL most valuable player, retired in February 2023 after 23 seasons in the NFL, having won six of his Super Bowl titles with the New England Patriots and one with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Following the end of his playing career, he also acquired a stake Las Vegas Raiders, while also becoming part of the ownership group of the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces. On top of that, Brady's commitments also include him being a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports. He leaves with Birmingham top of the Championship on goal difference with 29 points after 15 games. item.title: Ravens QB Jacoby Brissett’s status as Week 10 starter confirmed by Jesse Minter
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Ravens QB Jacoby Brissett’s status as Week 10 starter confirmed by Jesse Minter appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Losers of four in a row, the Baltimore Ravens will turn to Jacoby Brissett in an effort to save their season. Acquired from the Arizona Cardinals a few days ago, Brissett is slated to become the Ravens’ starting quarterback. Head coach Jesse Minter confirmed to reporters that Brissett is expected to start on Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers. Team beat reporter Jeff Zrebiec shared the news via X, formerly Twitter. “I expect him to be our starter Monday night,” Minter stated to the press. In the wake of season-ending injuries to starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano started the Ravens’ Thursday Night Football matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The 33-10 defeat to Jacksonville dropped the Ravens to 4-5, last in the AFC North. However, Baltimore is only two and a half games behind the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, who lead the division at 6-2. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Can Brissett lead the Ravens not only to the top of the AFC North, but the playoffs as well? Baltimore will face the Chargers next Monday night, followed by road trips to Carolina and Houston before their bye week. Fagnano only passed for 60 yards in the loss to Jacksonville, with two interceptions on 10-of-18 passing. If the former UConn standout is to succeed in the NFL, spending time behind Brissett could be a good thing. The veteran signal caller is well travelled, with stints playing for six different NFL franchises, including the Cardinals. Post-bye, the Ravens schedule doesn’t get any easier. After hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at the beginning of December, Baltimore will close out its season with four straight divisional matchups. That includes home and away matchups against the Steelers, the Ravens’ most hated rival. If Brissett can get into a rhythm quickly, then Baltimore certainly has a shot to climb their way back into the division race. Will Minter and Brissett get the Ravens back into playoff shape? If not, then fans will continue to wish that Jackson was under center once again. item.title: Bills place Josh Palmer on injured reserve
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Joshua Palmer #5 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball to score a 43 yard touchdown against the Detroit Lions during the first quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills wide receiver Josh Palmer injured his hamstring on Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens. We knew it was probably going to be a multi-week injury pretty soon after the game, and the Bills made it official Monday placing Palmer on injured reserve. He could be back after Thanksgiving. WR Tyrell Shavers and S Jordan Hancock are practicing on their way back from IR and one of them will likely take the roster spot. The Bills elevated Trent Sherfield for Monday night’s game and Skyler Bell is in line to see more snaps, as well. Sherfield is a candidate to join the 53-man roster, as well. The Bills can still trade Palmer ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline if they find a partner. The NFL changed the rules about trading players on injured reserve in 2018. A move like that would clear a not insignificant chunk of cap space for them to make another move. Palmer has four catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns in 2026. He played 12 games in 2025, catching 22 passes for 303 yards. A pretty expensive miss for the Bills and Brandon Beane to this point.

item.title: Patriots Must Fix Run Game Or Watch Maye Struggle Again
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images The New England Patriots lost Sunday, and they got their asses kicked in a big way. The final score read 45-27 against the Green Bay Packers, a result that leaves no room for excuses. Head coach Mike Vrabel did not sugarcoat the reality for his team or the fans watching at home. “We lost, and we got our asses kicked. There’s no two ways around it,” Vrabel said after the game on Sunday. The running game failed to provide any balance when the team needed it most. Rhamondre Stevenson, the centerpiece of the backfield, walked off the field with a knee injury and never returned to the contest. The team now faces a major question mark regarding their primary rusher just days before a trip to Germany. “I’m not sure the extent of what it is. He just came off, so we’ll take a look at it, and we’ll see. I don’t want to speculate right now,” Vrabel added in his postgame comments reported by Sports Illustrated . item.description: SAN ANTONIO, TX - DECEMBER 30: Texas Christian University Horned Frogs head coach Sonny Dykes talks with Mark Tommerdahl against the Southern California Trojans during the Valero Alamo Bowl football game at the Alamodome on December 30, 2025 in San Antonio, TX. item.title: Monday Musings: Notre Dame postmortem; adios, ACC title game
item.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 07: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes reacts against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the first half at Notre Dame Stadium on November 07, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Monday. It is not a victory Monday. That said, I hope you all are still doing well today. Let’s get down to brass taxes. 1) The Hurricanes proved they can still win without Malachi Toney. But it’s going to be a whole lot more along the lines of “hold on to your butts” fashion. I honestly believe the Canes win on Saturday if Toney is on the field. I don’t think that’s a wild take. Miami was an arguably shitty call away from tying it up without him. But Miami is mortal indeed over the next three games without him. The ground game was very underwhelming against a Notre Dame defense that was missing A TON of talent, including their interior DL duo. That’s what worries me the most. And Miami’s OL got their asses whipped in pass pro. Not quite Miami whipping Notre Dame’s ass in 2025 type of whipped, but still, the Irish won both sides of the line of scrimmage, and there isn’t much doubt about that. Miami NEEDS to get back to running the ball, and that starts will creating better running lanes and better overall production on the ground, however that happens. 2) I do not know what a catch is. You don’t. College football doesn’t. The NFL doesn’t. I have seen multiple attempts to interpret it through the supposed rules. And it’s always hinged on an “act common to the game”. Well, that includes taking another step. Elija Lofton took another step before the ball was dislodged from his hands. Apparently complying with that rule doesn’t matter. So, again, nobody knows what a catch is. Just catch the ball, hold it through the ground, take a nap, do your taxes, and maybe it’ll stand. Honestly, the thing that pisses me off more is no DPI call on the play before where Daylyn Upshaw’s arm was CLEARLY grabbed and he couldn’t sky to attempt to grab the pass. That was unequivocally interference and would have set up first and goal. Not even up for reasonable debate. But I’ll do what FSU fans can’t, and I’ll say that there’s absolutely no guarantee at all Miami wins if that happens. That likely ties the game up, and Notre Dame gets it back looking to score. Who knows what happens. 3) Now, back to the ACC, I ran the math, and Miami can clinch a spot in THE FINAL ACC title game on Saturday. Here’s what needs to happen: Miami needs to win, obviously. Wake Forest needs to beat SMU. North Carolina needs to beat Louisville. If those things happen, the only ACC teams with less than three ACC losses would be Miami, Wake, and Clemson. Clemson, at best, will finish 6-2 in the ACC. Miami, at worst with a win over Duke, would finish 7-2 in the ACC. Miami beat Clemson, as well as Wake. Miami clinches. 4) And yes, this will be it for the ACC Championship game, per the conference. Last one, best one 🏆 The 2026 ACC Foo

item.title: Why Eagles are trading Jordan Davis to Jaguars in blockbuster deal
item.description: Why Eagles are trading Jordan Davis to Jaguars in blockbuster deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles are having a nightmare 2026 NFL season. Heading into their Week 10 bye, the Eagles are currently 2-7, and there's not much hope for a second-half turnaround without Jalen Hurts. So, with the Eagles clearly headed towards one of the top picks in the 2027 NFL Draft, it would also make sense to hear that the Eagles are sellers. But what might not make sense to some is the stunning trade reported by ESPN's Adam Schefter . He reported that the Eagles are trading fan-favorite defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars . This is a massive trade for the Eagles, but there's a good reason why Howie Roseman has made this deal. Why the Eagles are trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars "Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN," Schefter reports. This is a major move for the Eagles, as the rumors surrounding Moro Ojomo being unavailable for trade make sense, but maybe not in the way fans might've expected. After trading Davis, the Eagles will now likely look to retain Ojomo for the foreseeable future. Davis, meanwhile, heads to the Jaguars and lands a massive haul of picks for Roseman and the Eagles. The Eagles had three elite defensive tackles with Ojomo, Davis, and Jalen Carter. It was always going to be unrealistic to keep all three. So, instead of letting Ojomo walk in free agency, or trading him or Carter, the Eagles decided to trade Davis. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade While he's a fan-favorite DT, the Eagles were given a very intriguing option with this massive trade offer from the Jaguars. A 2027 first-round pick is incredibly appealing, and getting a 2029 second-rounder is something maybe only Howie Roseman has the confidence to accept. Sure, losing Davis stings, but the Eagles were always going to lose a DT at some point. Now, Roseman can focus on signing Ojomo while using the first-round pick to add more cost-controlled help to this roster. Between the potential to sign Ojomo to an extension and the strong draft capital, this surprising trade made by the Eagles is one that does make some sense. item.description: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update (Monday): Sean McVay told reporters on Monday that Puka Nacua is likely headed to Injured Reserve with MCL and PCL sprains, plus a turf toe injury. Puka Nacua had a monster game for the Los Angeles Rams during Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The wide receiver hauled in 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, and added another 20 yards on a pair of rushing attempts, as the Rams moved above .500 on the season. But now Los Angeles is holding its collective breath, as Nacua is set for an MRI after injuring his knee on the Rams’ final offensive play of the game. According to Adam Schefter of ESPN, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to “determine the extent of the injury.” Schefter and Mike Garafolo are reporting that the team “does not elieve he suffered a torn ACL,” but that the “imaging Monday will tell more.” You can see that final offensive snap here: All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 The play was on of Nacua’s two rushing attempts on the game, an end-around design that was held to a short gain. Nacua did get up right after the tackle, but walked back to the sideline rather gingerly. Los Angeles plays the Arizona Cardinals in Week 10, before a bye week in Week 11. At times this season, Dias has been imperious, on others he has looked lost and slow. However, the hole in Manchester City’s midfield is not doing Dias any favours. Surely a system change or a tightening up of the City midfield will help Dias. Lastly, Vitor Reis has only been used sparingly this season. The Brazilian centre-back has a bright future and looms as the future of the Manchester City defence. With his pace and ability to read the game, there is a strong case to be made for Vitor Reis to play a more prominent role in the City defence. The case against Reis is that he isn’t yet physically mature enough to play consistently in the Premier League. item.title: Jaguars trade for Eagles’ Jordan Davis in massive NFL trade deadline blockbuster
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars have made a major move ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, acquiring defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles. Jacksonville is sending significant draft capital to Philadelphia as it continues strengthening its defense for a postseason push. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the blockbuster first. The Jaguars will send the Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Davis. “ This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today,” Schefter reported. He also noted that Philadelphia now has 10 picks across the first two rounds of the next three drafts. MORE: Jaguars make deal with Saints ahead of NFL trade deadline The move represents an aggressive approach from Jacksonville, which entered the deadline with a 6-2 record. Davis becomes another major addition to a defense that already welcomed safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. Eagles move Jordan Davis as Jaguars strengthen defense Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis (90) at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Davis joined Philadelphia as a first-round selection in the 2022 NFL Draft. The Georgia product became an important part of the Eagles’ defensive line during his time with the team. His departure is particularly surprising after Philadelphia signed him to a three-year, $78 million contract extension earlier this year. He had recorded 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks through nine games this season. However, the Eagles have struggled badly in 2026, falling to a 2-7 record. The franchise now appears focused on building future draft capital rather than making an immediate playoff push. The trade gives Philadelphia valuable selections to reshape its roster. General manager Howie Roseman will have additional flexibility across upcoming drafts. MORE: Jaguars acquiring Jessie Bates in trade with Falcons The price paid by Jacksonville reflects its urgency to compete now. The Jaguars are leading the AFC South and have built momentum under head coach Liam Coen. Davis brings size and experience to the defensive front. His arrival should help Jacksonville improve its interior pass rush and run defense. The Jaguars have made their intentions clear. They are willing to spend future draft capital to strengthen their playoff chances this year. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: White reflects on decision to leave 2022 World Cup – and says he is ‘immensely proud’ to be back playing for England
item.description: White reflects on decision to leave 2022 World Cup – and says he is ‘immensely proud’ to be back playing for England Arsenal defender Ben White has opened up on his decision to leave the England camp during the 2022 World Cup, admitting it is a choice he would “probably” make again. White left the Three Lions squad during the tournament and has largely remained silent on the circumstances surrounding his departure. “It’s something I haven’t spoken about, and I won’t go into detail about it,” White told TalkSport after being named in Thomas Tuchel’s latest squad . “It’s a decision I don’t want to talk about in a negative way or throw anyone under the bus. “It wasn’t an ideal situation but it’s probably one I would still make.” White has now returned to the England set-up under Tuchel and says he is delighted to be back with the national team. “Obviously, it’s amazing to be back in camp in a fresh moment ahead of the two games,” he said. Asked to clarify whether he had refused to play for England following the incident four years ago, White said: “There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn’t great. “I don’t want to throw anyone under the bus. A lot of people try to do that to me so it’s something I don’t want to do myself.” The Arsenal defender also addressed the criticism and boos he faced following his return to the England fold, insisting those responsible were unaware of the full circumstances surrounding his previous absence. “Especially because they didn’t know the situation, which is kind of what I put my mind to,” he said when asked how difficult the reaction had been. “They don’t know my situation, so it’s not really about what I’ve done because they don’t actually know why. “And I think if they did, they probably wouldn’t be booing or saying these things.” White says his overriding emotion following his England return is one of pride, particularly given the work he has put in away from public view. “It’s such a different feeling, I’m just immensely proud,” he said. “I think of what I’ve done to get in this position that no one has seen. “So, just taking a step back and being proud of how much I’ve done to get into this situation.”

item.title: Barcelona make fresh contact over deal for German international
item.description: Barcelona make fresh contact over deal for German international The brass at La Liga giants Barcelona have made contact with their counterparts at Bundesliga champions Bayer Munich, over a potential transfer deal. This comes amid the understanding that the Blaugrana have set their sights on the signature of Jonathan Tah. Stopper Tah has for his part been tipped for a potential Camp Nou switch on multiple occasions over recent seasons. In the summer of 2025, the German international swapped Bayer Leverkusen for Bundesliga rivals Bayern Munich, since playing an important role in Bavaria. As alluded to above, though, the interest of Deco and co. in a move for Tah has evidently not yet waned. As per a report from German transfer insider Florian Plettenberg: ‘FC Barcelona are looking for an experienced centre-back for January to partner Pau Cubarsí and have made an enquiry about Jonathan Tah. Deco and Hansi Flick continue to rate Tah highly.’ It is also noted, though: ‘However, a move is currently not an option for him. FC Bayern are also not willing to let him leave in January.’ Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Jordan Davis trade: Eagles acquire Jaguars’ first-round pick
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles were expected to be dealers ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, but they still surprised everyone with news they are sending team captain Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The move gives the Eagles another first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a second-rounder in 2029 — totaling 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next 3 drafts. Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 There had been speculation that the Jaguars were interested in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter — with Jacksonville being reportedly aggressive to add an interior defensive lineman after Jeffrey Simmons was traded by the Titans —, but the team didn’t want to move on from JC. Instead, it seems they were okay getting rid of Davis, who had risen to being a leader in the locker room. The Eagles had just signed Davis to a new, big-money contract back in March, 3-years for $78 million. The team made the move to re-sign Davis after he had shown extreme commitment to being in the best shape possible, and for the energy he brought to the defense, and even to special teams. Now, Davis will be saying goodbye to the team and city that drafted him, and will look to make a big impact for the Jaguars who are going all-in on their 2026 run. Through Week 9, they are 6-2, and made two other big trades ahead of the NFL’s deadline on Tuesday, November 10. Davis will always been appreciated for his time in Philly, and contributing to a top defense that won a Super Bowl, in addition for everything he did on and off the field. The Eagles told teams heading into the deadline that they were trying to keep Moro Ojomo and re-sign him after the season, so this move will give them more incentive to do so to keep the team strong up front.

item.title: Dan Campbell talks Lions OG Christian Mahogany after benching
item.description: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell was curt answering questions about Christian Mahogany on Monday, Nov. 9, but indicated the offensive lineman has a path to regain his starting job. “Yeah, listen, we’re good,” Campbell said when asked how Mahogany can repair his standing within the team. “I mean, I talked to him this morning, so the ball’s in his court, so all good.” The Lions benched Mahogany for Sunday’s win over the Miami Dolphins for an undisclosed violation of team rules. LET'S MAKE A DEAL: Lions add some security at safety with trade for Andre Cisco Miles Frazier started at left guard in Mahogany’s place, and Mahogany played only five snaps as a blocker, on field goal and extra point attempts. Campbell said Mahogany is not a trade candidate before Tuesday’s 4 p.m. NFL trade deadline, though he declined to say who his starting left guard is currently. The Lions could get starting center Cade Mays back from an ankle injury for their game against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday (9:30 a.m., CBS). Both he and fill-in center Juice Scruggs have previous experience at guard. Asked if Mahogany is back in the starting lineup or what he has to do to get there, Campbell said, “No, I just – the ball is in his court. That's all I said.” Injury update on D.J Reed, DJ Wonnum Campbell said it’s too early to know if the Lions will have cornerback D.J. Reed and defensive end DJ Wonnum back against the Patriots. Reed missed the Dolphins game with a hip injury, while Wonnum suffered a brain injury in the Lions’ Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings and remains in concussion protocol. “Yeah, hard to say. It really is,” Campbell said. “I mean, they've improved from last week. The question is can we get them there in time? And I don't have that answer right now.” Rock Ya-Sin started in Reed’s place at outside cornerback opposite Roger McCreary against the Dolphins, while rookie Derrick Moore had two sacks in his first NFL start in place of Wonnum. item.content:encoded: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell was curt answering questions about Christian Mahogany on Monday, Nov. 9, but indicated the offensive lineman has a path to regain his starting job. “Yeah, listen, we’re good,” Campbell said when asked how Mahogany can repair his standing within the team. “I mean, I talked to him this morning, so the ball’s in his court, so all good.” The Lions benched Mahogany for Sunday’s win over the Miami Dolphins for an undisclosed violation of team rules. LET'S MAKE A DEAL: Lions add some security at safety with trade for Andre Cisco Miles Frazier started at left guard in Mahogany’s place, and Mahogany played only five snaps as a blocker, on field goal and extra point attempts. Campbell said Mahogany is not a trade candidate before Tuesday’s 4 p.m. NFL trade deadline, though he declined to say who his starting left guard is currently. The Lions could get starting center Cade Mays back from an ankle injury for their game against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday (9:30 a.m., CBS). Both he and fill-in center Juice Scruggs have previous experience at guard. Asked if Mahogany is back in the starting lineup or what he has to do to get there, Campbell said, “No, I just – the ball is in his court. That's all I said.” Injury update on D.J Reed, DJ Wonnum Campbell said it’s too early to know if the Lions will have cornerback D.J. Reed and defensive end DJ Wonnum back against the Patriots. Reed missed the Dolphins game with a hip injury, while Wonnum suffered a brain injury in the Lions’ Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings and remains in concussion protocol. “Yeah, hard to say. It really is,” Campbell said. “I mean, they've improved from last week. The question is can we get them there in time? And I don't have that answer right now.” Rock Ya-Sin started in Reed’s place at outside cornerback opposite Roger McCreary against the Dolphins, while rookie Derrick Moore had two sacks in his first NFL start in place of Wonnum. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
item.description: WSL’s second-highest goalscorer is likened to England legend for her crossing and has earned France call-up At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
